first.rationale: Two of the three current problems are funnel-health problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%), and the inherited record points at onboarding simplification as the lever that touches both: memory_86 ties shorter onboarding to completion and time-to-value, and memory_31 ties field reduction at signup to a durable first-week activation lift. That is a compounding, retention-safe mechanism, which is what the primary objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue) asks for. I am deliberately not choosing promotional_pricing even though it is the most direct answer to the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records acquisition and revenue lift but a material 30-day retention drop, with an explicit instruction not to generalize it. Discounting into a price war would buy top-line accounts that churn, degrading exactly the metric I am optimizing, and it would also mask the underlying funnel regression rather than fix it. Activation messaging (memory_91) is the credible runner-up but addresses only the downstream symptom; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) and referral_incentive (memory_57) do not speak to the current regressions. Verification spend goes to memory_86 and memory_31 because they are the two memories my chosen action rests on, and both carry unresolved uncertainty: memory_31 is the oldest record here (day 12) and was measured on SMB accounts under pre-competitor conditions, so its lift may not transfer to today's traffic mix; memory_86 is a consolidated summary whose original effect size, duration, and whether the gain persisted past first week are not visible in the summary. I want the source records to confirm the effect was durable rather than a novelty bump, and to check whether either was run against a comparable baseline. I am not verifying memory_73 because its cautionary content is already decision-relevant as written and confirming it would not change my action. Standard experiment scale with a holdout: the mechanism is well-supported enough not to need a tiny guarded probe, but the two supporting memories are inherited summaries rather than fresh measurements, so I will not treat this as settled and will not go to broad rollout before reading out retention and qualified-revenue effects, not just completion rate. If verification shows either memory was weaker or narrower than summarized, I will fall back to activation_messaging.
